mechanism: Federal Reserve Bank of New York primary-dealer standards expect each primary dealer to bid in every U.S. Treasury auction for at least its pro-rata share of the offered amount at reasonably competitive prices. Treasury auctions have pre-announced security, size and competitive close, creating a dated institutional inventory-risk transfer in which designated dealers cannot simply opt out without jeopardizing primary-dealer standing.
claim: The primary-dealer participation expectation creates a causally explicit, pre-announced balance-sheet and inventory constraint around Treasury auctions. A separately authorized later test could ask whether a frozen auction-specific expression captures a repeatable concession associated with warehousing and distributing auction supply; no return or concession effect is claimed here.
prediction: Before outcome access, official documents should establish the offered amount, auction clock, primary-dealer population, pro-rata participation expectation, competitive-bid rules and a point-in-time instrument mapping. Failure to reconstruct these fields before the auction blocks test design.
falsification_scope: Mechanism usability is falsified if the primary-dealer expectation is not operationally binding enough to create meaningful inventory exposure, if customer/direct demand absorbs supply such that dealer exposure is not inferable ex ante, or if a candidate expression requires auction results or post-auction prices to define itself. A later negative economic test would falsify only the frozen expression, not the documented participation expectation.

decision_map.constraint: Primary dealers are expected to bid in every Treasury auction for at least a pro-rata share of the offered amount, at reasonably competitive prices, as an ongoing condition of the counterparty relationship.
decision_map.clock: Treasury announcement fixes the auction date and competitive close; competitive bidding usually closes at 1:00 p.m. ET, with security-specific schedules published in advance.
decision_map.affected_universe: Marketable U.S. Treasury bills, notes, bonds, TIPS and FRNs auctioned under public Treasury terms; any later test must freeze one instrument/tenor family before outcome access.
decision_map.capacity_intuition: Auction sizes are large, but actual dealer inventory risk is reduced by direct and indirect customer demand, pre-auction when-issued trading, hedging, syndication-like distribution and deep Treasury liquidity. Gross issuance is not equivalent to dealer net exposure.
implementability_questions: Can auction announcements, offered amount, competitive close and instrument identifiers be archived point-in-time?
Can the contemporaneous primary-dealer count be reconstructed before each auction without hindsight?
Can an expression be specified using only announcement/when-issued information and not auction results?
How should direct and indirect bidder demand be treated when it is unknown before the close?
Can financing, bid-ask, hedge and balance-sheet costs be frozen before outcome access?
active_disconfirmation: The New York Fed standard is an expectation governing the counterparty relationship, not a statutory obligation to receive a fixed allocation; dealers can bid at reasonable competitive levels and may receive less inventory than the pro-rata bid amount.
Treasury auctions are open to direct and indirect non-dealer demand, so primary dealers need not warehouse the full marginal supply.
When-issued markets allow pre-auction risk transfer and price discovery, potentially eliminating any systematic concession before the auction.
The mechanism can therefore be structurally real while producing no capturable alpha after financing, hedging, spread, impact and competition.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York — Primary Dealers
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Primary dealers are expected to bid on a pro-rata basis in all Treasury auctions at reasonably competitive prices; pro-rata is total amount auctioned divided by the number of primary dealers.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York — Primary Dealer Operating Policy
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Primary-dealer standards are ongoing counterparty expectations, including traditional primary-dealer functions.
Treasury auctions are regular and announced in advance; competitive bids generally close at 1 p.m. ET and awards are determined by the auction rule.
Auction announcements publish security, amount, auction date, issue date, maturity and closing times; competitive awards are capped at 35% per customer.

legacy_distinctness.screen_scope: Current repository Legacy/research artifacts and frozen hypotheses searched for Treasury auction, primary-dealer, forced-flow and institutional-rebalance mechanisms before freeze.
nearby_but_distinct: Russell reconstitution benchmark flow: equity index-tracking constraint at a closing auction rather than dealer participation in sovereign issuance
month-end pension rebalance: asset-allocation flow rather than primary-market dealer auction obligation
generic rates/carry mechanisms: price/factor exposures rather than a designated-counterparty auction participation constraint

next_validator_decision.PASS_TO_TEST_DESIGN: Official auction and dealer-status data permit a fully point-in-time expression defined before auction results or prices are inspected.
next_validator_decision.PARK_DATA: Mechanism is documented but the required point-in-time when-issued/financing or dealer-population inputs cannot be reconstructed without leakage.
next_validator_decision.KILL_MECHANISM: Participation expectations do not imply a sufficiently measurable ex-ante inventory constraint or any admissible expression necessarily depends on auction outcomes.
